sections.text: Perturbation theory expands the scattering matrix as a sum of Feynman diagrams. External lines are incoming or outgoing particles. Internal lines are propagators, the amplitude for a virtual particle to travel between two points; a virtual particle is one that appears only inside a diagram, never as an external line. Vertices are interaction points. Momentum is conserved at each vertex, and undetermined loop momenta are integrated over. A virtual boson of mass m produces a force of range R ≈ ħ/(mc). Example: for the neutral pion of mass 135 MeV, using ħc = 197 MeV fm, R ≈ 197 ÷ 135 ≈ 1.46 fm. Loop diagrams give divergent integrals.

sections.heading: Gauge theories and renormalisation
sections.text: A gauge theory is invariant under a symmetry transformation that varies from point to point. Demanding this local invariance requires gauge fields, the force carriers, and a covariant derivative. Quantum electrodynamics is the U(1) case. Yang-Mills theories have non-Abelian groups. Spontaneous symmetry breaking can give gauge bosons mass through the Higgs mechanism. Loop divergences are absorbed by renormalisation into a finite number of measured parameters, such as masses and couplings. The remaining predictions are finite, and couplings run with energy, meaning their strength changes with the energy of the process.

sections.heading: Standard Model
sections.text: The Standard Model is a gauge theory with group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1). SU(3) is quantum chromodynamics, the theory of quarks and gluons. SU(2)×U(1) is the electroweak theory, broken by the Higgs field to electromagnetism. Matter comes in three generations of quarks and leptons. The model includes the photon, W and Z bosons, gluons and the Higgs boson. It does not include gravity, and it does not fully explain neutrino masses or dark matter.

keyPoints: Canonical quantisation promotes a field to an operator and imposes equal-time commutation relations, such as [φ(x), π(y)] = iδ³(x − y), or anticommutation relations for fermions.
Feynman diagrams organise perturbation theory: external lines are particles, internal lines are propagators, and vertices are interactions.
The range of a force from exchange of a virtual boson of mass m is about R ≈ ħ/(mc); for the 135 MeV neutral pion this gives about 1.46 fm.
A gauge theory requires gauge fields and a covariant derivative to keep the theory invariant under local symmetry transformations.
Renormalisation absorbs loop divergences into a finite set of measured parameters and makes couplings run with energy.
The Standard Model is the gauge theory SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1), and it does not include gravity.

en.title: Many-body physics in condensed matter
en.short: Second quantisation, electron gas, phonons, superconductivity and many-body phenomena.

sections.heading: Second quantisation
sections.text: Second quantisation treats the wavefunction as an operator. For each single-particle state k, a creation operator a†_k adds a particle and an annihilation operator a_k removes one. The occupation number n_k = a†_k a_k counts particles in that state. Fermions obey {a_k, a†_k'} = δ_kk' and {a_k, a_k'} = 0; bosons obey [a_k, a†_k'] = δ_kk'. In a solid, k labels band and wavevector. The Hamiltonian becomes H = Σ ε_k a†_k a_k plus interaction terms. This notation makes many-particle states and interactions compact.

sections.heading: Interacting electron gas
sections.text:
The electron gas has kinetic energy and Coulomb repulsion. Hartree-Fock theory adds exchange, which lowers the energy of parallel spins. Screening weakens the long-range Coulomb force. Low-energy excitations behave as quasiparticles with renormalised mass, described by Fermi liquid theory. Plasmons are collective charge oscillations at ω_p = √(n e²/(ε0 m)).

Example: for n = 1.0 × 10²⁸ m⁻³, E_F = (ħ²/2m)(3π²n)^(2/3) = 1.69 eV. This is a typical metallic value.

sections.heading: Phonons and collective modes
sections.text: Phonons are quantised lattice vibrations. Acoustic phonons have frequency tending to zero as wavevector q tends to zero; optical phonons have a finite frequency at q = 0. The Debye model cuts off the spectrum at ω_D. Electron-phonon coupling lets electrons scatter and pair. Plasmons, spin waves (magnons) and zero sound are other collective modes. Their dispersion reveals the underlying interactions.

sections.heading: Superconductivity
sections.text: In BCS theory, electrons form Cooper pairs through a phonon-mediated attraction. Below the critical temperature T_c, pairs condense and open an energy gap Δ. The weak-coupling result is Δ = 2ħω_D exp(−1/N(0)V), where N(0) is the density of states at the Fermi level and V is the pairing strength. Superconductors expel magnetic flux (Meissner effect) and show Josephson tunnelling. Other many-body phenomena include the Kondo effect, quantum Hall states and Mott insulators.

keyPoints: Second quantisation uses creation and annihilation operators; fermions anticommute, {a_k, a†_k'} = δ_kk', and bosons commute, [a_k, a†_k'] = δ_kk'.
The interacting electron gas combines kinetic energy with Coulomb repulsion; screening and exchange lead to quasiparticles and Fermi liquid behaviour.
The free-electron Fermi energy is E_F = (ħ²/2m)(3π²n)^(2/3); for n = 1.0 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ it is about 1.69 eV.
Phonons are quantised lattice vibrations; acoustic modes vanish at long wavelength, optical modes do not.
Plasmons oscillate at ω_p = √(n e²/(ε0 m)).
BCS theory predicts Cooper pairing and a gap Δ = 2ħω_D exp(−1/N(0)V) below T_c.

en.title: Research methods and dissertation in physics
en.short: Planning, ethics, data management and writing a physics dissertation, plus oral exam preparation.

sections.heading: Research design
sections.text:
Start with a clear research question and a testable objective. Decide whether the work is experimental, computational, theoretical or observational, and choose methods that can answer the question. Define variables, controls, sample size and calibration. Check feasibility: time, equipment, skills and cost.

A useful case: Amina tests whether annealing temperature changes the efficiency of thin-film solar cells. She fixes the measurement protocol, makes replicated samples and records instrument settings, so differences can be attributed to temperature rather than drift.

sections.heading: Literature and proposal
sections.text:
A literature review is an argument, not a list. Read original papers and reviews, compare methods and results, and state the gap your work addresses. Keep search terms and references in a citation manager (reference software).

A proposal usually gives background, aim, objectives, method, timeline, resources, risks and ethics. Make each objective specific enough to assess. Discuss feasibility with your supervisor before submission.

sections.heading: Ethics and data
sections.text:
Get ethics approval before collecting data if your work involves people, animals or sensitive information. Physics projects may also need safety approval for lasers, radiation, chemicals or high voltage. Rules differ by country and institution, so check your committee early.

Write a data management plan: what you will collect, file formats, metadata (information about the data), storage, backup, access and retention. Record work in a dated lab notebook and use version control (change tracking) for code. Good records make results reproducible (repeatable by others) and support your thesis.

sections.heading: Writing and viva
sections.text:
Structure the dissertation around the argument: abstract, introduction, theory, methods, results, discussion, conclusion and references. State limitations honestly. Write for an examiner who is intelligent but not a specialist in your exact topic.

For the oral examination, prepare a short talk, reread your thesis and anticipate questions about method, errors and alternatives. Practise with your supervisor or peers. Never bluff; say what you know and how you would check the rest. Thesis and examination rules vary, so read your university’s current regulations.

keyPoints: A research question should determine whether the project is experimental, computational, theoretical or observational.
A literature review must identify a gap and justify your method, not merely summarise papers.
A proposal should state aim, objectives, method, timeline, resources, risks and ethics.
Obtain ethics and safety approval before data collection; requirements vary by country and institution.
A data management plan covers formats, metadata, storage, backup, access and retention.
In the viva, explain your choices and limitations honestly and check current university regulations.
